summary: The legal bound has at most 16 decimal digits, which is too narrow for an honest runtime-scaling verdict; the accepted implementation counts shorter lengths and scans the bound's digits once.

replacement_checks.evidence: The accepted source creates at most 16 decimal characters, sums at most 15 shorter-length terms, and processes each of the at most 16 bound digits once, establishing O(D) time over the complete legal width bound.

The dedicated regression compares the accepted adapter with an independent incremental zero-free counter for every n through 1,000,000, then checks decimal-width boundaries and deterministic values across the full legal range.
